issues.description: The problem statement, template, and tests expect a PersonService method named addParent(Person, Person). In the solution repository PersonService the implemented method is named registerParent(Person, Person) while other artifacts in the solution (PersonResource and tests) still call addParent. This name/signature mismatch across artifacts will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct API to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align method naming across artifacts. Either rename registerParent(...) in the solution's PersonService to addParent(...), or add a public addParent(Person person, Person parent) method that delegates to registerParent. Ensure all references (PersonResource, tests, and problem statement guidance) consistently use the same method name and signature.

issues.description: The conceptual operation 'add a parent to a person' is referred to as addParent in the problem statement, the template, and the tests/resources, but the solution implementation uses the different method name registerParent in PersonService. This divergence breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the described requirement (addParent), the template stubs, and the final implementation, and may cause confusion or failing references (e.g., PersonResource and tests call addParent while the service defines registerParent).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the operation across all artifacts. Rename registerParent in PersonService to addParent (matching the problem statement, template stubs, PersonResource, and tests), or add an addParent wrapper that delegates to registerParent so that both names are available and consistent with the specified API.
